chain.label: Promech's risk-tolerant organizational culture and lack of a formal safety program
chain.trigger: Promech's company culture, which tacitly endorsed flying in hazardous weather and failed to manage the risks associated with the competitive pressures...; its lack of a formal safety program

chain.label: Inadequate operational control: no joint pilot/scheduler concurrence obtained before flight release
chain.trigger: no such explicit concurrence occurred between the accident pilot and the flight scheduler (or any member of company management) before the accident flight. As a result, the decision to initiate the accident tour rested solely with the accident pilot

caused_by.evidence: Promech's training and supervision of the flight scheduler...was insufficient to ensure that she fully understood and was performing her responsibilities to work jointly with the pilots

chain.label: Class B TAWS alerting thresholds mismatched to low-altitude float operations
chain.trigger: the float-equipped accident airplane was authorized...to cruise over the surface as low as 500 ft agl, which is below the Class B TAWS design alerting threshold

chain.label: TAWS caution/warning/advisory alerts left inhibited on the accident airplane
chain.trigger: data recovered from the accident airplane's EFIS recorded that the TAWS CWA alerting function was set to the inhibit position at the time of impact

caused_by.evidence: frequent nuisance alerts during tour operations prompted them to inhibit the alerts

chain.label: Pilot chose the riskier short overland route instead of the safer overwater route
chain.trigger: the pilot's decision to fly a riskier, overland route despite marginal weather conditions and the availability of a safer, overwater route was influenced by schedule pressure and his attempt to emulate the behavior of other, more experienced pilots

caused_by.evidence: Promech management fostered a company culture that tacitly endorsed operating in weather conditions that were below FAA minimums
the decision to initiate the accident tour rested solely with the accident pilot

chain.label: Flight encountered deteriorating weather over the southern half of Ella Lake
chain.trigger: the accident flight encountered deteriorating weather conditions over the southern half of Ella Lake, and, at the time of the accident, the terrain at the accident site was likely obscured by overcast clouds with visibility restricted in rain and mist

caused_by.evidence: the accident flight encountered deteriorating weather conditions over the southern half of Ella Lake

chain.label: Pilot continued visual flight into the area of instrument meteorological conditions
chain.trigger: the pilot's decision to continue visual flight into an area of instrument meteorological conditions

caused_by.evidence: the pilot continued the flight into near-zero visibility conditions

chain.label: Geographic disorientation caused pilot to mistake the first mountain for the second and turn west early
chain.trigger: the pilot's route deviation placed the airplane on a collision course with a 1,900-ft mountain, which it struck at an elevation of about 1,600 ft mean sea level

caused_by.evidence: which resulted in his geographic disorientation and controlled flight into terrain

chain.label: Ineffective last-second aggressive pitch-up upon recognizing the collision course
chain.trigger: as soon as he realized that the flight was on a collision course with the terrain, he pulled aggressively on the elevator flight controls in an ineffective attempt to avoid the terrain

caused_by.evidence: the airplane began to pitch up rapidly, experiencing about +2 Gs of vertical acceleration and climbing before it collided with terrain

chain.label: Airplane collided with mountainous, tree-covered terrain
chain.trigger: the airplane had collided with a near-vertical rock face in a nose-high, wings-level attitude at an elevation of about 1,600 ft msl

caused_by.evidence: the nuisance alerts and associated increase in the use of the inhibit mode prevent TAWS from effectively providing the intended protection

chain.label: Fatal injuries to the pilot and all eight passengers
chain.trigger: the commercial pilot and eight passengers sustained fatal injuries, and the airplane was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: based on the damage and high loads sustained during the impact sequence, the accident was not survivable
